title: Anchor email send answered 500 on a transient SMTP AUTH reply and turned a gate flow red
summary: On 2026-11-17 at 12:09Z the dev Anchor API answered `500 EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED` to one of four parallel email sends in the flow `Parallel email sends reach the right email step`, so the anchor flow suite ran 34/35. The SMTP relay of the suite product had answered AUTH with `454 4.7.0 Temporary authentication failure` after 11 s, and no layer of Anchor retries a transient 4yz reply. It was the seventh such reply since 2026-11-06, all on dev; the shared ledger had filed the first six as `expected` and never escalated them. The flow is in the `anchor` gate tag, so the same reply during a deploy would hold Anchor's prod promotion. The rerun went green at 12:26Z. Anchor now retries a transient AUTH reply once on a fresh connection, before any message is sent. On 2026-11-20 at 01:52Z it recurred during an Echopoint gate: the caller hung up after 10 s, its resend got the in-flight record as `201`, and the provider skipped its one AUTH retry because the request context was already cancelled, so the send ended `FAILED` behind that `201`. The dispatch now runs on a bounded context detached from the request.

impact.text: Dev only, no customer saw it. One red suite run; no gate ran during it, so prod promotion was not held this time. Seven failed email sends on dev since 2026-11-06, each recorded as a FAILED send. The 2026-11-20 recurrence lost one more dev send behind a `201` duplicate during an Echopoint gate run.

trigger: The suite product's SMTP relay answered AUTH with `454 4.7.0 Temporary authentication failure: Connection lost to authentication server` while the flow sent four emails in parallel.
detection: The routine's suite run (`run_suites.sh`) printed `FAILED anchor db6c38bb …: status_code equals expected=201 actual=500` at the end of the anchor tag, 5 minutes after the send. The six earlier replies were seen by the log routine (`grafana-watch`) within hours, but the ledger status `expected (watch)` kept them out of the postmortem loop, so detection of the pattern took 11 days.
resolution: A rerun of the flow went green at 12:26:45Z. anchor#395 (merged 12:35:45Z as 0ce3dbb6) makes the Anchor SMTP provider redial and re-authenticate once when AUTH answers 4yz; no message has been sent at that point, so the retry cannot send twice. A relay outage longer than one retry still fails the send, and a gate-tagged real-SMTP flow still holds prod on it (A3). The 2026-11-20 recurrence showed the retry ran on the request context, so a caller that hung up cancelled it; the follow-up PR dispatches on a context detached from the request and bounded to 60 s, proven by a component test that ended `FAILED` before the change and `SENT` after.

whys.problem: The anchor flow suite went red on dev, and a gate run at that moment would have held Anchor's prod promotion

because.evidence: Node result of execution `01a1e969`; VictoriaLogs `POST …/email/sends -> 500 (11.210764s)` at 12:09:36Z

because.text: The SMTP relay answered AUTH with `454 4.7.0 Temporary authentication failure` after 11 s
because.evidence: VictoriaLogs `failed to send email: smtp auth: 454 4.7.0 …` at 12:09:36.242Z; the three other parallel sends got 201

because.text: Anchor fails the send on any AUTH error; nothing retries a 4yz reply, which RFC 5321 marks transient
The provider comment says the email service owns retry, and the service has no retry, so each layer assumed the other retried
because.evidence: Comment on `Send`: 'The email service is responsible for rendering, idempotency, and retry'; `SendStatusFailed` says 'failed permanently after retries'; no retry in `email/service`

because.text: No layer owns retry of a transient SMTP reply, and no test covers a 4yz AUTH reply
Six earlier 454 replies since 2026-11-06 produced no fix, so the seventh reached a gate-tagged flow
because.evidence: Ledger row `logs:dev:anchor:failed to send email: smtp auth: 454 …`, count 6, status `expected (watch)`

because.text: The ledger status `expected (watch)` is not one of the loop's known states, so a repeat only appended a note
because.evidence: `postmortem-loop.md` §1 lists open, fix-awaiting-review, fix-merged, fix-live, verified; the row grew six notes, each deferring to a human

because.text: The postmortem loop has no rule that escalates a repeating `expected` error to a postmortem
A caller that times out before the relay answers gets a 201 duplicate while the first send ends FAILED
because.evidence: Sixth occurrence 2026-11-14T12:16:45Z: resend with the same dedupe key answered 201 in 2 ms; the first attempt got 454 at 11.7 s

because.text: Delivery runs inside the caller's request, so a slow relay is the caller's wait and the caller's failure
because.evidence: `emailService.Send` dispatches with the request context and only detaches the status write

because.text: Email dispatch is synchronous to the API request; there is no queued delivery, so a slow relay is the caller's wait
The 2026-11-20 recurrence: the dispatch ran on the request context, so the caller's hang-up cancelled the provider's AUTH retry
because.evidence: 01:52:51.098Z warn `retrying once`, 5 ms later `failed to send email` 454 and `-> 499 (11.037s)`; `dialAndAuthenticate` returns the 454 on `ctx.Done()`

because.text: anchor#395 added the retry inside the request lifetime, and its tests drove `Send` with a live context; no test hung up the caller
because.evidence: `provider_send_retry_test.go` calls `Send(context.Background(), …)`; no component test cancels a send request

because.text: `emailService.Send` detached only the status write from the request, not the dispatch it records

contributing: The suite product sends real mail through a third-party relay, so the relay's availability is a gate input.
A 500 is not a transport error, so neither `run_suites.sh` nor the Deploy Router gate reruns the flow.

well: The suite run caught the failure on its first pass, and the node result plus VictoriaLogs gave the cause in two queries.
The four parallel sends showed the failure was one relay reply, not a routing bug in the flow's subject.
wrong: Six occurrences over 11 days were filed as expected; each run deferred the same design question without opening a draft PR.
The `Send` comment promised a retry that did not exist.
The ledger marked the row verified while A3 stayed open, so a known open cause first read as a regression.
The A1 retry was tested only with a caller that waits; the failure the sixth occurrence had already shown (a caller that hangs up) had no test.
lucky: No Deploy Router gate ran at 12:09Z; the same reply during a gate would have held Anchor's prod promotion.
All seven replies hit dev; VictoriaLogs shows no 454 AUTH reply on prod since 2026-11-01.
On 2026-11-20 the duplicate `201` kept the Echopoint gate green; without the resend the gate would have gone red and held prod, and with it a real user would have lost the email silently.

actions.what: SMTP provider redials and re-authenticates once on a 4yz AUTH reply; unit tests for 454→235, 454→454 and 535
postmortem-loop.md and grafana-watch.md: a repeating `expected` or `noise` row (second time in 14 days, or reaching a suite or gate) gets a postmortem
Decide on queued email dispatch with bounded retries, so a slow relay does not block the caller (ADR); the detached dispatch shipped as A5
Alert on `failed to send email` with an SMTP 4yz cause on prod
Dispatch on a context detached from the request and bounded to 60 s; component test `TestEmailSendFinishesAfterClientHangUp` (caller hangs up, relay answers 454 then 235, record ends SENT)

messaging.internal: Dev anchor suite went red on one email send: the SMTP relay answered AUTH 454 (transient) and Anchor does not retry it. Rerun green. Fix: one AUTH retry on a fresh connection. Queued dispatch needs a design decision.
